page.description: Kali Linux editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: Debian-based and rolling, built around the security toolset. The installer image is the one to write if you want a full Kali system on the disk.
pros: The security toolset is installed and updated from one repository.
Rolling release: no reinstalls between point images.
Debian base, so the usual Debian knowledge carries over.
Xfce 4.20.8 and kernel 7.1 in this build.
cons: A rolling image: no end-of-life date is published.
The toolset is large; this installer ISO is 5 GB.
Not a general-purpose desktop first; expect security-focused defaults.
The Commons screenshot shows an older Kali desktop.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of a Kali Linux desktop from Wikimedia Commons. It is not 2026.3 and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted for this page.

shot.alt: Kali Linux Xfce desktop with the application menu and a terminal
shot.caption: Stock screenshot of a Kali desktop · not 2026.3, no USB written, no boot tested.

page.status: One image pinned here: the amd64 installer ISO, written with dd or any image writer. Writing erases the stick; the installer then partitions or erases the target disk. Kali is rolling and publishes no end-of-life date.

editions.description: The full installer: it puts Kali on the disk with the toolset, instead of running live from the stick.
